author: Ifmyante
text:
That's a really good and important question.

The issue you raised can be the difference between success and failure.

I've just finished a webinar with the Academy. We discussed the same
stuff we discuss in every webinar, yet the attendees still seemed to get
 a lot out of it.

This means that for many, learning comes from repetition.

Now, when we talk in the Academy, we can be talking about one topic, yet
 we remain mindful of all the other topics which have an influence on
price.

It can take years to be able to see it all at once. Some get it in a couple of months, sure, but for most it's a long journey.

The Academy Lite is made to be different.

Let's use a metaphor.

We want to make a cup of tea.

In the Academy, to do this, we teach about the electricity which powers
the kettle, the specific heat capacity of water and metal, the bimetalic
 strip which turns off the kettle, the latent heat of vapourisation of
water, how tea is grown, distributed, sold and stored, everything about
milk, sugar, etc.

In the Academy Lite, we'll teach how to fill a kettle, let it boil,
throw a teabag into a cup, pour water and add milk and sugar to taste.

Both can achieve exactly the same results. It's just that one gives a greater understanding of the process.

So, for the beginning of the lesson, all charts will be hand drawn. But we'll then move on to real chart based examples.

I've kept the drawing of levels as simple as possible, so that a trading system can easily be formed.

This means that students will have more losses than the Academy
students, sure, but our money management lesson will make sure that
overall profits can easily be made.

So, if you want to know the basics of how to make a perfect cup of tea, this is the place to go

Disclaimer: We will not be teaching how to make tea, but let me say that Earl Gray with milk and two sugars is absolutely lovely

author: MarkN
text:
That's an excellent analogy! Making a cup of tea for Academy students
is about knowing at exactly what temp. to heat the water and for
precisely how long to leave the bag inside the cup for the tea to have
its fullest expression of flavour. What's common are the ingredients and
 the tools, but the results produced from understanding the art of
flavour will be different from those who follow the recipe. However in
saying this, I also realize that by making the tea I may not get the
perfect results all the time when I apply basic principles, as such
results come from a deeper understanding of the variables influencing
the process.
